q: Other things remaining the same, a lower Turnover Ratio of stores generally indicates:

options.A: Excessive stocking of stores in depots
options.B: A larger proportion of dead surplus in the stock held
options.C: Better turnover of the capital locked up in stores
options.D: Heavy outstanding balances under Purchase Suspense

e: A lower Turnover Ratio means a smaller stock is held relative to issues, which indicates better turnover of the capital locked up in stores.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 5,000 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 125 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 5 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity is:
A continuously mounting debit balance in the Stock Adjustment Account of a railway is a matter of concern because it indicates:

options.A: Recurring losses and differences in stores accounting which require investigation and control
options.B: That the stores balance of the railway is increasing
options.C: That the Turnover Ratio of stores is improving
options.D: That purchases are being made at favourable rates

e: A continuously mounting debit balance in the Stock Adjustment Account indicates recurring losses and differences in stores accounting which require investigation and control.

q: Receipts of stores into depots are, in the first instance, accounted for in the General Books of the railway under:

options.A: The final revenue heads of the consuming departments

e: Receipts of stores into depots are, in the first instance, accounted for in the General Books under Stores Suspense, the stock account.

q: A depot holds 400 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 30 per unit. A fresh receipt of 200 units is taken into stock at Rs 45 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item will be:
e: Revised average rate = (400 x 30 + 200 x 45) / 600 = 21,000 / 600 = Rs 35 per unit.

q: Certain stores, such as coal and oils, are subject to normal losses in handling and transit. Shortages of such stores within the prescribed permissible limits are:

options.A: Recovered in full from the stockholder in all cases
options.B: Adjusted by write-off under the sanction of the competent authority
options.D: Carried forward indefinitely under a suspense head

e: Shortages of stores such as coal and oils within the prescribed permissible limits are normal handling and transit losses, adjusted by write-off under the sanction of the competent authority.

q: Stores transferred from a depot of one zonal railway to a depot of another zonal railway are priced at:

options.B: The book rate of the receiving railway
options.C: The book rate of the issuing railway
options.D: An assessed value fixed by the Railway Board

e: Stores transferred from a depot of one zonal railway to a depot of another are priced at the book rate of the issuing railway.

q: The AAC of an item is 4,800 units. The stock in hand is 400 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 200 units. The coverage available for the item is:
e: Coverage = (stock in hand + dues) / AAC x 12 = (400 + 200) / 4,800 x 12 = 1.5 months.

q: Samples of stores such as oils, paints, chemicals and metals, where testing is prescribed before acceptance, are tested in:

options.C: The office of the Tender Committee
options.D: The Chemical and Metallurgical laboratory of the railway

e: Samples of stores such as oils, paints, chemicals and metals, where testing is prescribed before acceptance, are tested in the Chemical and Metallurgical laboratory of the railway.

q: The maximum consumption of an item is 150 units per week and the maximum lead time for its procurement is 8 weeks. The re-order level of the item is:
e: Re-order level = maximum consumption x maximum lead time = 150 x 8 = 1,200 units.

q: The powers of stores officers to accept tenders and sanction purchases of stores are laid down in:

options.A: The personal discretion of the officer concerned
options.D: The delegation of powers under the Model Schedule of Powers (SOP)

e: The powers of stores officers to accept tenders and sanction purchases are laid down in the delegation of powers under the Model Schedule of Powers (SOP).

q: If the total issues of stores of a railway increase substantially while the closing stores balance remains unchanged, the Turnover Ratio will:
e: Turnover Ratio varies inversely with issues: if total issues increase substantially while the closing balance remains unchanged, the ratio decreases.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,500 units and the re-order quantity is 1,000 units. The minimum consumption is 40 units per week and the minimum lead time is 5 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:
e: Maximum level = re-order level + re-order quantity - (minimum consumption x minimum lead time) = 1,500 + 1,000 - 40 x 5 = 2,300 units.

q: As a general rule, payment for stores purchased by the Railways is made:

options.A: In advance, on placement of the purchase order
options.B: On despatch of the material by the supplier
options.C: At the end of the financial year
options.D: Only after receipt, inspection and acceptance of the stores at the destination

e: As a general rule, payment for stores purchased is made only after receipt, inspection and acceptance of the stores at the destination.

q: In the Priced Stores Ledger, a separate folio (account) is maintained for each stores item identified by its:
e: In the Priced Stores Ledger, a separate folio is maintained for each stores item identified by its PL (Price Ledger) number.

q: The average consumption of an item is 120 units per week. Its average lead time is 5 weeks, but the lead time may extend up to 8 weeks. The safety (buffer) stock to be provided against lead-time variation is:
e: Safety stock against lead-time variation = average consumption x (maximum - average lead time) = 120 x (8 - 5) = 360 units.

q: A Receipt Note is prepared by a stores depot for stores received from:

options.A: All sources — purchases, workshop manufacture, transfers from other depots and returns from departments/works

e: A Receipt Note is prepared for stores received from all sources - purchases, workshop manufacture, transfers from other depots and returns from departments or works.

q: Under a stores contract, stores of the value of Rs 3,00,000 remain in arrear of supply and are supplied 5 weeks late. Liquidated damages at 0.5 per cent of the value of the stores in arrear for each week of delay amount to:
e: Liquidated damages = 0.5% of Rs 3,00,000 per week = Rs 1,500 per week; for 5 weeks = Rs 7,500.

q: The head of account to which the value of an issue of stores is to be debited is indicated on the:
e: The head of account to which the value of an issue of stores is to be debited is indicated on the Issue Note.

q: A supplier's bill for stores amounts to Rs 12,00,000. The advance payment admissible at 98 per cent of the bill value, against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, is:
e: Advance payment = 98% of Rs 12,00,000 = Rs 11,76,000.

q: On completion of stock verification of an item, the stock sheet showing the difference between the physical and book balances is signed by the stockholder:

options.A: In token of his having seen and noted the difference recorded
options.B: As an admission of personal liability in all cases
options.C: Only when an excess is found in the stock
options.D: Only when directed by the Railway Board

e: On completion of stock verification, the stockholder signs the stock sheet in token of his having seen and noted the difference recorded between the physical and book balances.

q: A depot holds on an average 5,000 units of an item whose book rate is Rs 80 per unit. The inventory carrying cost is estimated at 18 per cent per annum of the value of stock held. The annual inventory carrying cost of the item is:
e: Stock value = 5,000 units x Rs 80 = Rs 4,00,000; annual carrying cost = 18% of 4,00,000 = Rs 72,000.

q: The value of stores held in the depots of a railway is reflected in the Balance Sheet of the railway as:

options.D: It is not reflected in the Balance Sheet at all

e: The value of stores held in the depots is reflected in the Balance Sheet of the railway as an asset (stock in hand).

q: A supplier fails to supply 1,000 units of stores contracted at Rs 120 per unit. A risk purchase of the same quantity is made at Rs 135 per unit. The extra cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:
e: Extra cost of risk purchase = (135 - 120) x 1,000 = Rs 15,000, recoverable from the defaulting supplier.

q: Besides IREPS, railway stores tenders are published on the:

options.D: Notice board of the depot only

e: Besides IREPS, railway stores tenders are also published on the Central Public Procurement (CPP) Portal.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 55 lakh, receipts of stores during the year are Rs 2.2 crore and issues during the year are Rs 2.05 crore. The closing balance of stores is:
e: Closing balance = opening balance + receipts - issues = 55 lakh + 2.2 crore - 2.05 crore = Rs 70 lakh.

q: Before a risk purchase is effected against a defaulting supplier, the original purchase order is, in respect of the quantity in default:

options.A: Kept open indefinitely till the supplier chooses to supply
options.B: Cancelled (short-closed) for the defaulted quantity, after giving due notice to the supplier

e: Before a risk purchase is effected, the original purchase order is cancelled (short-closed) for the defaulted quantity, after giving due notice to the defaulting supplier.

q: A depot holds 1,500 units of an item. The book rate of the item is revised from Rs 60 to Rs 52 per unit. The decrease in the value of the stock in hand, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:
e: Decrease in stock value = 1,500 units x (60 - 52) = Rs 12,000, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: Stores drawn from a depot for the execution of a capital work are:

options.A: Debited to the account of the work concerned
options.D: Held under Sales Suspense till the work is completed

e: Stores drawn from a depot for the execution of a capital work are debited to the account of the work concerned.

q: The minimum level of an item is 500 units and the maximum level is 2,500 units. The average stock level of the item is:
e: Average stock level = (minimum level + maximum level) / 2 = (500 + 2,500) / 2 = 1,500 units.

q: Heavy outstanding debit balances under Purchase Suspense (bills paid but material not received) tend to:

options.A: Understate the stores balance of the railway
options.B: Inflate the closing stores balance and thereby the Turnover Ratio
options.C: Improve the Turnover Ratio of stores
options.D: Have no effect on the stores balance

e: Heavy outstanding debit balances under Purchase Suspense inflate the closing stores balance, and thereby the Turnover Ratio, since bills are paid but the material is not yet received into stock.

q: The AAC of an item is 9,000 units. Coverage for six months is to be provided. The stock in hand is 800 units and the dues are 700 units. The quantity to be ordered is:
e: Six months' requirement = 9,000 / 12 x 6 = 4,500 units; less stock in hand 800 and dues 700, the quantity to be ordered = 3,000 units.

q: A stores depot issues 600 units of an item whose book rate is Rs 55 per unit. The value of the issue debited to the consuming department is:
e: Value of the issue = 600 units x Rs 55 per unit = Rs 33,000.

q: In ABC analysis, the annual consumption value of an item, used for its classification, is worked out as:

options.A: Stock in hand multiplied by the unit price of the item
options.B: Annual consumption in units multiplied by the unit price of the item
options.C: Annual consumption in units divided by the unit price of the item
options.D: Maximum stock level multiplied by the unit price of the item

e: In ABC analysis, the annual consumption value of an item = its annual consumption in units multiplied by its unit price.

q: The re-order level of an item is 800 units. The average consumption is 60 units per week and the average lead time is 10 weeks. The minimum stock level of the item is:
e: Minimum stock level = re-order level - (average consumption x average lead time) = 800 - 60 x 10 = 200 units.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Surplus stores are serviceable stores held in a depot in excess of its requirements, which may be of use to some other depot or railway.
2. Scrap stores are stores which have become unserviceable and are fit only to be disposed of as scrap.
e: Both statements are correct: surplus stores are serviceable stores held in excess of a depot's requirements which may be of use elsewhere, while scrap stores are unserviceable and fit only to be disposed of as scrap.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 4,900 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 100 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 2 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity of the item is:
Non-stock stores purchased against a specific demand of a work or department are accounted for by:

options.A: Taking them into the priced stock of the depot like stock items
options.B: Crediting their value to Purchase Suspense
options.C: Including them in the closing balance of stores of the railway
options.D: Charging their cost direct to the work or department concerned, without routing them through the stock accounts

e: Non-stock stores purchased against a specific demand are charged direct to the work or department concerned, without routing them through the stock accounts.

q: Under the periodic review (periodic ordering) system of inventory control:

options.A: A fixed quantity is ordered whenever the stock falls to the re-order level
options.B: Stock is reviewed at fixed intervals and an order is placed to restore the stock to a predetermined target level
options.C: Orders are placed only when the stock is completely exhausted
options.D: The supplier reviews the stock position and despatches material automatically

e: Under the periodic review system, stock is reviewed at fixed intervals and an order is placed to restore the stock to a predetermined target level.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Advance payment up to 98% of a stores bill is made against the inspection certificate and proof of despatch, before the stores are actually received at the depot.
2. The balance 2% of the bill is paid after the stores have been received, inspected and accepted at the destination depot.
e: Both statements are correct: the 98% advance is paid against the inspection certificate and proof of despatch before receipt, and the balance 2% is paid after the stores are received, inspected and accepted at destination.

q: A depot holds 600 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 20 per unit. A fresh receipt of 400 units is taken into stock at Rs 35 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item will be:
e: Revised average rate = (600 x 20 + 400 x 35) / 1,000 = 26,000 / 1,000 = Rs 26 per unit.

q: Where only a part of the quantity ordered in a purchase order has been received and accepted at the depot, the supplier's bill is passed for payment:

options.A: For the full quantity ordered, as the purchase order is a concluded contract
options.B: Only for the quantity actually received and accepted
options.C: For 98% of the full order value in all cases
options.D: Only after the entire quantity ordered has been received

e: Where only a part of the quantity ordered has been received and accepted, the supplier's bill is passed for payment only for the quantity actually received and accepted.

q: A tender for stores could not be decided within the period of validity of the offers. The tender can thereafter be accepted:

options.A: At any time, as the tenderer remains bound by his offer indefinitely
options.B: Only after forfeiting the earnest money of the tenderer
options.C: Only by inviting fresh tenders in every such case
options.D: Only with the consent of the tenderer, who may refuse to extend the validity of his offer without forfeiting his earnest money

e: Once the validity of offers has expired, the tender can be accepted only with the consent of the tenderer, who may refuse to extend the validity of his offer without forfeiting his earnest money.

q: Stores supplied by a firm which do not fully conform to the specification, but are usable for the intended purpose, may be accepted:

options.A: By the competent authority under a deviation, with a suitable reduction in price
options.B: By the depot storekeeper at the full contract price
options.C: Only if the supplier agrees to replace them during the warranty period
options.D: In no circumstances; such stores must always be rejected

e: Stores not fully conforming to the specification but usable for the intended purpose may be accepted by the competent authority under a deviation, with a suitable reduction in price.

q: In a stores contract, liquidated damages for delayed supply are levied at 0.5% of the value of the stores in arrear per week of delay, subject to a maximum of:
e: Liquidated damages for delayed supply are levied at 0.5% of the value of the stores in arrear per week of delay, subject to a maximum of 10% of the contract value.

q: Where extension of the delivery period is granted to a supplier for delayed supply of stores:

options.A: Liquidated damages can thereafter never be levied in any case
options.B: The grant of extension does not by itself absolve the supplier from liquidated damages, unless the extension is granted specifically without levy of liquidated damages
options.D: The security deposit of the supplier is automatically forfeited

e: The grant of extension of the delivery period does not by itself absolve the supplier from liquidated damages, unless the extension is granted specifically without levy of liquidated damages.

q: The 'stock-out' (shortage) cost of a stores item refers to:

options.A: The cost of storing the item in the depot
options.B: The price paid for the item to the supplier
options.C: The cost of placing an order for the item
options.D: The losses and extra costs arising when an item is not available in stock when demanded, such as idle time of men and machines and emergency purchase at higher prices

e: Stock-out cost refers to the losses and extra costs arising when an item is not available in stock when demanded, such as idle time of men and machines and emergency purchase at higher prices.

q: In inventory control, the 'service level' of a stock item denotes:

options.A: The proportion of demands for the item which are met promptly from stock
options.B: The number of years for which the item remains serviceable
options.C: The percentage of the stock of the item verified during the year
options.D: The proportion of the item supplied by local suppliers

e: In inventory control, the service level of a stock item denotes the proportion of demands for the item which are met promptly from stock.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Stores transferred from one depot to another depot of the same railway are priced at the book rate, without addition of departmental charges.
2. Stores issued to outside parties and other Government departments are priced at the book rate plus the prescribed departmental charges.
e: Both statements are correct: transfers between depots of the same railway are priced at the book rate without departmental charges, while issues to outside parties and other Government departments are priced at book rate plus the prescribed departmental charges.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the priced accounts, each issue of stores is valued at the purchase rate of the oldest lot held in stock, following the first-in-first-out method of pricing.
2. Issues of stores are valued at the prevailing (average) book rate of the item, irrespective of the lot from which the material is physically drawn.
e: Statement 2 is correct: in the priced accounts, issues of stores are valued at the prevailing average book rate of the item, not lot-wise on the first-in-first-out method, so statement 1 is wrong.

q: Where stores are issued from a railway depot to a contractor for use on a work being executed by him:

options.A: No charge is made for the stores, as they belong to the Railway
options.B: The value of the stores is recovered in cash from the contractor before issue
options.C: The value of the stores is written off to the Stock Adjustment Account
options.D: The value of the stores, at the rates prescribed in the contract, is debited to the work and recovered from the amounts payable to the contractor

e: Stores issued to a contractor for a railway work are not free; their value at the rates prescribed in the contract is debited to the work and recovered from the amounts payable to the contractor.

q: Besides the Stores Officer and the Finance member, a Stores Tender Committee includes:

options.A: A representative of the indenting (user) department, for technical evaluation of the offers
options.B: A representative of the lowest tenderer
options.C: The depot storekeeper of the consignee depot
options.D: A nominee of the Railway Board in every case

e: A Stores Tender Committee combines the Stores Officer, the Finance member and a representative of the indenting department, whose technical knowledge is needed to evaluate whether the offers meet the user's requirement.

q: A purchase order placed on a supplier contains certain special conditions which are inconsistent with the IRS Conditions of Contract. In such a case:

options.A: The IRS Conditions of Contract prevail and the special conditions are void
options.B: The special conditions incorporated in the purchase order prevail over the general (IRS) conditions
options.C: The purchase order itself becomes void
options.D: The matter must be referred to the Railway Board in every case

e: Special conditions deliberately written into a purchase order are a conscious departure from the general IRS conditions, and as the specific terms of that contract they prevail over the general conditions.

q: Under the periodic system of inventory, as distinct from the perpetual inventory system followed on the Railways:

options.A: Stock balances are known continuously from the records after every receipt and issue
options.B: Bin cards and priced ledgers are updated after every transaction
options.C: The quantity of stock in hand is ascertained only by physical count at intervals, and not continuously from records
options.D: No physical verification of stock is necessary at all

e: Under the periodic system, the quantity in hand is found only by physical count at intervals, so balances are not known continuously from records; the perpetual system, by contrast, tracks every receipt and issue.

q: Where a supplier offers quantity discounts for bulk purchase of an item, the decision whether to avail of the discount is taken by:

options.A: Always accepting the largest quantity, as the unit price is the lowest
options.B: Comparing only the ordering costs at each quantity
options.C: Comparing only the carrying costs at each quantity
options.D: Comparing the total cost — purchase cost, ordering cost and carrying cost — at the Economic Order Quantity and at each price-break quantity

e: A quantity discount lowers unit price but raises average stock and carrying cost, so the decision is taken by comparing total cost - purchase, ordering and carrying - at the EOQ and at each price-break quantity.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. At the Economic Order Quantity, the annual ordering cost and the annual inventory carrying cost of an item are equal.
2. At the Economic Order Quantity, the total purchase price payable for the item over the year is also the minimum.
e: Statement 1 is true: at the EOQ the falling ordering cost and rising carrying cost are equal, which is what makes total cost minimum. Statement 2 is false, as the total purchase price depends on quantity and price, not on the EOQ.

q: On the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), payment to the seller for stores supplied is processed after the consignee generates the:
e: On GeM, the consignee generates the CRAC after receiving and accepting the goods; this acceptance certificate is what triggers processing of the payment to the seller.

q: Procurement of stores by single tender, otherwise than against a Proprietary Article Certificate, can be resorted to only:

options.A: When the stores officer finds an open tender inconvenient
options.B: For all purchases below the two-packet tender threshold
options.C: With recorded justification and the sanction of the competent authority with finance concurrence
options.D: When only one firm is registered with the Railways for the item

e: Single tender without a PAC bypasses competition, so it is permitted only with recorded justification and the sanction of the competent authority with finance concurrence, keeping the exception accountable.

q: During stock verification, a shortage of 40 units of an item is found. The book rate of the item is Rs 275 per unit. The value of the shortage to be accounted for is:
e: Shortage value = 40 units x Rs 275 per unit = Rs 11,000, the shortage being valued at the book rate of the item.

q: Under a stores contract, stores of the value of Rs 5,00,000 remain in arrear of supply and are supplied 4 weeks late. Liquidated damages at 0.5% of the value of the stores in arrear for each week of delay amount to:
e: Liquidated damages = 0.5 per cent of Rs 5,00,000 = Rs 2,500 per week x 4 weeks = Rs 10,000, charged on the value of stores in arrear.

q: A supplier's bill for stores amounts to Rs 6,50,000. The advance payment admissible at 98% of the bill value, against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, is:
e: Advance payment = 98 per cent of Rs 6,50,000 = Rs 6,37,000, admissible against the inspection certificate and despatch documents before the stores are received.

q: The Turnover Ratio of the stores of a railway is 0.20 and the closing balance of stores is Rs 50 lakh. The total issues of stores during the year are:
e: Turnover Ratio = closing balance / total issues, so total issues = Rs 50 lakh / 0.20 = Rs 2.5 crore.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 75 lakh and the closing balance is Rs 45 lakh. The average stock held during the year is:
e: Average stock = (opening balance + closing balance) / 2 = (75 + 45) / 2 = Rs 60 lakh.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 85 lakh, receipts of stores during the year are Rs 1.9 crore and issues during the year are Rs 1.75 crore. The closing balance of stores is:
e: Closing balance = opening Rs 85 lakh + receipts Rs 1.9 crore - issues Rs 1.75 crore = Rs 1 crore.

q: The average value of stock held by a railway is Rs 60 lakh. If the inventory carrying cost is estimated at 25 per cent per annum of the average stock value, the annual inventory carrying cost is:
e: Annual carrying cost = 25 per cent of the average stock value of Rs 60 lakh = Rs 15 lakh.

q: The AAC of an item is 7,200 units. The stock in hand is 900 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 300 units. The coverage available for the item is:
e: Monthly consumption = 7,200 / 12 = 600 units; coverage = (stock in hand 900 + dues 300) / 600 = 2 months.

q: The average consumption of an item is 75 units per week, the lead time is 8 weeks and the safety (buffer) stock is 250 units. The re-order level of the item is:
e: Re-order level = average consumption x lead time + safety stock = 75 x 8 + 250 = 850 units.

q: The re-order level of an item is 2,000 units and the re-order quantity is 1,200 units. The minimum consumption is 80 units per week and the minimum lead time is 5 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:
e: Maximum level = re-order level + re-order quantity - (minimum consumption x minimum lead time) = 2,000 + 1,200 - (80 x 5) = 2,800 units.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,400 units. The average consumption is 110 units per week and the average lead time is 8 weeks. The minimum stock level of the item is:
e: Minimum level = re-order level - (average consumption x average lead time) = 1,400 - (110 x 8) = 520 units.

q: A stores depot issues 450 units of an item whose book rate is Rs 48 per unit. The value of the issue debited to the consuming department is:
e: Issue value = 450 units x Rs 48 per unit = Rs 21,600, debited to the consuming department at the book rate.

q: A supplier fails to supply 800 units of stores contracted at Rs 95 per unit. A risk purchase of the same quantity is made at Rs 112 per unit. The extra cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:
e: Extra cost of risk purchase = (Rs 112 - Rs 95) x 800 units = Rs 13,600, recoverable from the defaulting supplier.

q: The maximum consumption of an item is 180 units per week, its normal consumption is 150 units per week and the lead time is 6 weeks. The safety (buffer) stock to be provided for the item is:
e: Safety stock = (maximum consumption - normal consumption) x lead time = (180 - 150) x 6 = 180 units, covering consumption above normal during the lead time.

q: The annual requirement of an item is 9,600 units and the quantity ordered each time (Economic Order Quantity) is 800 units. The number of orders to be placed during the year is:
e: Number of orders = annual requirement / EOQ = 9,600 / 800 = 12 orders in the year.

q: The Economic Order Quantity of an item is 900 units and its safety stock is 300 units. If the inventory carrying cost is Rs 16 per unit per year, the annual carrying cost of the average inventory held is:
e: Average inventory = EOQ/2 + safety stock = 450 + 300 = 750 units; annual carrying cost = 750 x Rs 16 = Rs 12,000.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 3,500 units and its book rate is Rs 240 per unit. For the purposes of ABC analysis, the annual consumption value of the item is:
e: Annual consumption value = 3,500 units x Rs 240 = Rs 8,40,000; ABC classification is based on this consumption value, not on quantity alone.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 1.10 crore, receipts of stores during the year are Rs 2.6 crore and the closing balance is Rs 90 lakh. The total issues of stores during the year are:
e: Total issues = opening + receipts - closing = 1.10 + 2.6 - 0.90 = Rs 2.8 crore.

q: The opening debit balance under Purchase Suspense of a railway is Rs 8 lakh. During the month, stores bills amounting to Rs 30 lakh are paid and material worth Rs 34 lakh is received at the depots and linked with the bills. The closing balance under Purchase Suspense is:
e: Purchase Suspense: opening debit Rs 8 lakh + bills paid Rs 30 lakh - material received and linked Rs 34 lakh = closing debit balance of Rs 4 lakh.

q: The minimum level of an item is 650 units and the maximum level is 1,850 units. The average stock level of the item is:
e: Average stock level = (minimum level + maximum level) / 2 = (650 + 1,850) / 2 = 1,250 units.

q: The safety (buffer) stock of a stores item:

options.A: Is included as a cost element in the Economic Order Quantity formula
options.B: Has the effect of reducing the re-order level of the item
options.C: Is ordered afresh along with every order for the item
options.D: Does not enter the Economic Order Quantity computation, but is taken into account in fixing the re-order level so that the buffer is available during the lead time

e: Safety stock does not enter the EOQ computation, which balances only ordering and carrying costs; it is instead taken into account in fixing the re-order level so the buffer is available during the lead time.

q: A stores item is treated as a 'stock item' of a depot when:

options.A: It is purchased only once for a specific work
options.B: It is regularly stocked in the depot for meeting demands, bears a Price Ledger (PL) number and has an AAC fixed for it
options.C: It has been held in the depot for more than 24 months
options.D: It is supplied free of cost by a contractor

e: A stock item is one regularly stocked in the depot for meeting demands, bearing a PL number and having an AAC fixed for it, unlike a non-stock item bought for a specific work.

q: Liquidated damages for delayed supply under a stores contract are levied on:

options.A: The total value of the purchase order, irrespective of the quantity supplied in time
options.B: The value of the stores remaining in arrear of supply, for the period of delay
options.C: The amount of the security deposit furnished by the supplier
options.D: The value of the stores actually supplied by the supplier

e: Liquidated damages are levied on the value of the stores remaining in arrear of supply for the period of delay, since only that portion has caused the loss, not the whole order.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 1,600 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 200 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 4 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity of the item is:
e: EOQ = square root of (2 x annual consumption x ordering cost / carrying cost) = square root of (2 x 1,600 x 200 / 4) = 400 units.

q: The Security Deposit furnished by a supplier under a stores contract is refunded to him:

options.A: After successful completion of the supplies and expiry of the warranty/guarantee period
options.B: Immediately on delivery of the stores at the depot
options.C: On issue of the purchase order to the supplier
options.D: Only after the close of the financial year in which the order was placed

e: The Security Deposit safeguards due performance, so it is refunded only after the supplies are successfully completed and the warranty/guarantee period has expired.

q: A depot holds 500 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 12 per unit. A fresh receipt of 300 units is taken into stock at Rs 20 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item will be:
e: Revised average rate = (500 x Rs 12 + 300 x Rs 20) / 800 units = Rs 12,000 / 800 = Rs 15 per unit.

q: Railway stores held in depots are ordinarily NOT insured with a commercial insurer because:

options.A: No insurance company accepts railway stores for insurance
options.B: The value of the stores is too small to be insured
options.C: Government follows the principle of bearing its own risks and does not ordinarily insure its own property
options.D: The stores are kept in fire-proof godowns in all depots

e: Government follows the principle of bearing its own risks and does not ordinarily insure its own property, so railway stores held in depots are not insured with a commercial insurer.

q: A stores depot issues 275 units of an item whose book rate is Rs 72 per unit. The value of the issue debited to the consuming department is:
e: Issue value = 275 units x Rs 72 per unit = Rs 19,800, debited to the consuming department at the book rate.

q: Other things remaining the same, if the cost of placing an order for a stores item decreases, the Economic Order Quantity of the item will:

options.D: Become equal to the annual consumption

e: EOQ rises with the ordering cost in its formula, so if the cost of placing an order decreases, smaller and more frequent orders become economical and the EOQ decreases.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 60 lakh and the total issues during the year are Rs 5 crore. The Turnover Ratio of stores is:
e: Turnover Ratio = closing balance / total issues = Rs 60 lakh / Rs 5 crore = 0.12.

q: A 'repeat order' in stores purchase means:

options.A: Re-inviting tenders for the same item a second time
options.B: Asking the supplier to repeat the inspection of the stores supplied
options.C: An order placed on the same supplier, at the same rates and terms as a recent order, for an additional quantity of the same item
options.D: Placing two orders for the same item on two different suppliers

e: A repeat order is placed on the same supplier at the same rates and terms as a recent order, for an additional quantity of the same item, without a fresh tender.

q: The average value of stock held by a railway is Rs 45 lakh. If the inventory carrying cost is estimated at 16 per cent per annum of the average stock value, the annual inventory carrying cost is:
e: Annual carrying cost = 16 per cent of the average stock value of Rs 45 lakh = Rs 7,20,000.

q: Which of the following is a recognised source from which stores may be obtained without inviting tenders?

options.A: Private firms recommended by the consuming department
options.B: Government departments and public sector undertakings
options.C: Firms offering the lowest rates in the open market
options.D: Foreign suppliers dealing directly with the Railways

e: Government departments and public sector undertakings are a recognised source from which stores may be obtained without inviting tenders, their supplies and rates being treated as reliable.

q: During stock verification, a shortage of 35 units of an item is found. The book rate of the item is Rs 180 per unit. The value of the shortage to be accounted for is:
e: Shortage value = 35 units x Rs 180 per unit = Rs 6,300, the shortage being valued at the book rate.

q: Before an order banning business dealings with a firm is issued, the firm is ordinarily:

options.A: Given an opportunity to show cause and explain its position
options.B: Required to deposit the full value of its pending orders
options.C: Struck off the list of registered firms without any notice
options.D: Debarred from participating in tenders for one year automatically

e: An order banning business dealings is a penal step, so the firm is ordinarily given an opportunity to show cause and explain its position before the order is issued.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 1.5 crore and the closing balance is Rs 1.1 crore. The average stock held during the year is:
e: Average stock = (opening balance Rs 1.5 crore + closing balance Rs 1.1 crore) / 2 = Rs 1.3 crore.

q: In stores procurement, a reverse auction on IREPS is conducted:

options.B: Among the tenderers whose offers have been found technically acceptable
options.C: Among all tenderers, including those whose offers have been rejected
options.D: Only among firms registered as micro and small enterprises

e: A reverse auction is a price contest among tenderers whose offers have already been found technically acceptable; rejected or unexamined offers cannot be allowed to bid.

q: Under a stores contract, stores of the value of Rs 4,00,000 remain in arrear of supply and are supplied 6 weeks late. Liquidated damages at 0.5 per cent of the value of the stores in arrear for each week of delay amount to:
e: Liquidated damages = 0.5 per cent of Rs 4,00,000 = Rs 2,000 per week x 6 weeks = Rs 12,000.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Pre-despatch inspection of stores is carried out at the supplier's premises before the material is despatched.
2. Where pre-despatch inspection is not prescribed in the purchase order, the stores are inspected by the consignee depot after their receipt.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: pre-despatch inspection, where prescribed, is done at the supplier's premises before despatch; where it is not prescribed, the consignee depot inspects the stores after receipt.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 70 lakh, receipts of stores during the year are Rs 2.4 crore and issues during the year are Rs 2.25 crore. The closing balance of stores is:
e: Closing balance = opening Rs 70 lakh + receipts Rs 2.4 crore - issues Rs 2.25 crore = Rs 85 lakh.

q: Before scrap is offered in an e-auction, an auction catalogue is published on the e-auction portal, which contains:

options.A: The names of the firms which will participate in the auction
options.B: Lot-wise details of the scrap offered for sale, with the place of the material and the conditions of sale
options.C: The sale price fixed for each lot by the Stores Department
options.D: The names of purchasers who defaulted in earlier auctions

e: The auction catalogue published before an e-auction gives lot-wise details of the scrap offered, the place where the material lies and the conditions of sale, for the information of bidders.

q: A supplier's bill for stores amounts to Rs 7,50,000. The advance payment admissible at 98 per cent of the bill value, against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, is:
e: Advance payment = 98 per cent of Rs 7,50,000 = Rs 7,35,000, admissible against the inspection certificate and despatch documents.
